blocks.content: I find painting spots by walking. No destination. Just moving until something stops me. Every time I've tried to plan it — this corner, that wall, that particular light — the result is worse than whatever I would have found if I'd just kept walking and paid attention.
My art teacher in middle school called it wandering with intention. My mom calls it not being able to commit to things. They're probably both right.
I took the back streets. The town was fully awake now — storefronts open, traffic steady, people moving with somewhere to be. I kept to the parts that still felt like morning.

There's a mural in the alley on Clement that I've been thinking about for a month. Someone painted it years ago, and the color has thinned in places, but the structure underneath is still good — a figure reaching for something just outside the frame, real ivy grown up over the left edge into painted ivy, the border between them going soft. I stop there most mornings. I've never actually set up there. I keep feeling like it's waiting for something to happen first.
I stopped. Looked at it for a while.
Then I thought about the bracelet catching the light. And the way she'd turned without looking back.
